topics.topic: Ownership and dependency direction for semantic validation of runtime settings
questions: Does `runtime_settings` own rejection of every value the A8 start-up table disallows, including an out-of-range integer port, an unknown time-zone name, and a value outside `RuntimeEnvironment`, or only failures of lexical parsing; if only lexical parsing, which module owns those semantic checks?

Does “wrong form” include every value rejected by A8—an out-of-range integer port, an unknown time zone, and a string outside RuntimeEnvironment—or only values that cannot be parsed into the declared type; and, if only parsing failures are included, which module owns the remaining refusals?

Does `runtime_settings` also own rejection of values that have the right form but violate A8, specifically a port outside 1–65535 and a syntactically valid time-zone name unknown to the time-zone database?

May `runtime_settings` know and query the time-zone database needed to enforce A8, or must that validation be supplied by another module; if another module supplies it, which module owns it and what is the dependency direction?

quotes: A8: a required setting is present, an optional one that is absent takes its decided default, and every value is one the start-up table accepts.
A port above 65535, an unknown time zone or an invalid connections file ends the start.
judgement.why: The later public-operation contracts assign rejection of every start-up-table violation to runtime_settings while also retaining deliverer_service's explicit checks for an above-range port and an unknown time zone, so implementations do not have to infer the validation behavior.

topics.topic: Exact accepted textual forms for environment-variable values
questions: What constitutes a wrong-form value for the required `str` path settings `binary_root`, `state_dir`, `connections_file`, and `credential_file`, given that path existence is explicitly outside this module and A8 supplies no lexical path grammar?
What exact textual forms are accepted for each environment variable, especially whether the port accepts signs, surrounding whitespace, leading zeroes, or non-ASCII decimal digits?

quotes:
- the default of each optional setting, and the refusal of a missing required setting or of a value of the
  wrong form.

Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read.
judgement.why: The lexical grammar, whitespace and numeral parsing rules, and whether an empty string is an accepted path value are input-format and public-contract details owned by State 6.

topics.topic: Whether an empty environment-variable value counts as a missing required setting
questions: Is a required setting missing only when its environment variable is absent, as A8 states, or also when the variable is present with an empty value?

quotes:
A required setting that
is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default.

- the default of each optional setting, and the refusal of a missing required setting or of a value of the
  wrong form.
judgement.why: Whether a present empty environment value is parsed as a value, treated as absent, or rejected as wrong-form is an input-format contract detail owned by State 6.

provenance.quote: A required setting that is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default.
